text:
Marathon Petroleum climbed 4% today, continuing a sharp rally that has added over 21% in two weeks. The immediate driver is rising oil prices—Brent crude topped $106 following a deadly attack on a Saudi airport and ongoing conflict concerns—combined with refineries running near capacity (92.7%) and relatively low diesel storage, which creates better margins for refiners to convert crude into saleable products.

The broader context is geopolitical uncertainty supporting energy prices: the Saudi-Houthi conflict, potential Russian diesel entering (or not entering) global markets depending on U.S. political decisions, and tension around Iran's nuclear sites all create an environment where crude stays elevated and refining capacity becomes more valuable. Refiners like Marathon benefit when oil prices rise faster than they can pass those costs through—a situation that has clearly held over the past two weeks.
